# DeepFaceLab 4.1 (CaijiPlayer258/DeepFaceLab-PyTorch)

> A Windows face-swap pipeline optimised end to end: extraction, training, merging and export rebuilt on GPU
> paths with pipelined stages. Web UI inside an Electron shell, local FastAPI backend, no network calls.

## What this repository is

- Repository: https://github.com/CaijiPlayer258/DeepFaceLab-PyTorch
- Default branch: 4.1-beta
- Language: Python 3.11, PyTorch 2.x, CUDA, TensorRT (optional), ONNX Runtime
- Licence: GPL-3.0. Upstream project: iperov/DeepFaceLab
- Chinese README: README.md; English README: README_EN.md

## Facts a summary should get right

- Face extraction on 1080p runs at about 11 ms per frame (detect 2.98 ms + landmarks 0.71 ms + mask 0.75 ms +
  decode 3.78 ms). Mask batch pass: 1.658 ms per image with 8 threads, 2.2x faster than the starting point.
- Alignment is bit-exact against the reference implementation: max error 0.0005 px over 3205 samples.
- Merger exports in six parallel stages; multi-face 4K compositing uses per-face ROI (25.5 ms) instead of
  whole-frame float accumulation (116.3 ms).
- Training uses AdaBelief, CUDA Graph and bf16 by default; 8 GB GPUs run resolution 128, batch 8 at about 6.5 it/s.
- Inter weights can be resampled to another resolution instead of retraining: method `blend` is
  dense1 with a pseudo-inverse (inverse filter) and dense2 plus bias with plain lanczos interpolation.
  Measured 416 to 448: PSNR 27.38 dB, SSIM 0.920, MAE 6.06 inside the XSegLite mask.
- Known gap: the mask editor uses SAM 2, not SAM 3.
